candidates.fit: Cortex-M0, SWD on PA13/PA14 with internal pull-up/down at reset, TRUE dedicated NRST and BOOT0 pins (no GPIO alt-function on either) - the most textbook STM32 pinout of the set. Best stock of any SWD candidate (19,015). BOOT0 has no internal pull, so it needs one external pull-down resistor (precedented in this repo's stm32-blinky board); internal 8MHz HSI runs and debugs with no crystal.

Pin-compatible STM32 clone, genuine ARM SWD on PA13/PA14 with internal pulls active at reset. BOOT0 (PF4) datasheet-documented internal pull-down - zero extra boot-strap parts. Cheapest ARM candidate, good stock (2,536), internal HSI (4-24MHz selectable) needs no crystal. Thinner official documentation/community maturity than genuine STMicro parts; datasheet's TSSOP20 pin table carries two sub-variants (F1/F2) not fully reconciled here.

Current-gen Cortex-M0+, SWD on PA13/PA14 (internal pulls at reset). BOOT0 rides the SWCLK pin (PA14-BOOT0) with its own internal pull-down defaulting to boot-from-flash - zero external boot-strap parts, leanest ST BOM here (VDD/VDDA and VSS/VSSA each merged to one pin). NRST (PF2) is itself GPIO-reassignable, a minor architectural note. Stock 1,371 still >>5, just thinnest of the three healthy SWD picks. Already smoke-tested live on this host.

Required non-ARM entry (WCH RISC-V). Best stock (16,813) and price of any candidate, leanest BOM of all five (single VDD/VSS pin pair, no BOOT0 pin exists at all). Debug is single-wire SWIO on PD1 (shared with a timer/ADC alt-function) - needs a WCH-Link-class probe, not the ST-Link/J-Link/DAPLink the brief names; community OpenOCD/PicoRVD/minichlink alternatives exist but aren't turnkey. Picking this part also reshapes J2 to one debug signal instead of two.

Not recommended. More capable Cortex-M0+ (64MHz/8KB RAM) with the same clean SWD + internal-pull-down BOOT0 story as STM32C011, but only 68 units in stock today (near-zero margin over a 5-board build) and this exact TSSOP20 pinout shares physical pads between unrelated signals (e.g. PA15/PA14-BOOT0), reducing simultaneous GPIO below the headline 18. Listed to show the same-vendor upgrade path exists, not a practical pick here.
